subject: Science
title: Caring for living things
objectives: Children will water plants and say that plants need water.
Children will show kind and gentle handling of animals.
content: Watering plants, feeding and caring for pets, and being kind and gentle to animals.
teachingActivities: Give each child a real job such as watering; talk about what each living thing needs; model gentle voices and hands; never leave children alone with real animals.
learnerActivities: Water plants, say what pets need and handle toy animals gently.
resources: A toy pet with a bowl
assessment: Observe whether each child waters a plant with support and handles a toy animal gently.

lessons.title: Watering plants
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will water plants and say that plants need water.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know that plants and animals are alive and need food, water and care.
resources: Two potted plants, one dry and one watered
lessons.starter: Show a droopy plant and say "This plant is thirsty. It needs a drink."
teacherActivities: Water the droopy plant slowly and say "Drink, plant."
Let each child water a small plant with the can.
Compare the two plants and ask "Which one is happy?"
learnerActivities: Child points to the watered plant.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Water the droopy plant slowly and say "Drink, plant." Children: Children watch and say water.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child water a small plant with the can. Children: Child waters the plant gently.
Step 3. Teacher: Compare the two plants and ask "Which one is happy?" Children: Child points to the watered plant.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We look after plants." Children: Children say the sentence.

practical.title: Water the plants
steps: Give each child a turn with the can.
practical.safety: Use small watering cans and shallow trays. Wipe spills straight away so no one slips.

differentiation.support: Hold the can together and pour slowly.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to water two plants and say which needs more.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the plants in the sun and say "Grow, plants."
lessons.homeConnection: Help to water a plant at home every day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "water plants and say that plants need water" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Looking after a pet
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will say what a pet needs and pretend to care for it.
successCriteria: Names two things a pet needs
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know that plants and animals are alive and need food, water and care.
resources: A bowl, a water dish and a blanket
Pictures of food, water, a bed and a walk
lessons.starter: Hold a toy dog and say "This is Rex. He is hungry and thirsty. What does he need?"
teacherActivities: Show the pictures and say what a pet needs: food, water, a bed.
Feed the toy pet and give it water.
Put the pet to bed with a blanket.
Ask "How do we look after a pet?"
learnerActivities: Children look and say the words.
Child feeds and gives water to the toy.
Child says or shows one way.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the pictures and say what a pet needs: food, water, a bed. Children: Children look and say the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Feed the toy pet and give it water. Children: Child feeds and gives water to the toy.
Step 3. Teacher: Put the pet to bed with a blanket. Children: Child tucks the pet in.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How do we look after a pet?" Children: Child says or shows one way.

practical.title: Pet care play
steps: Set up a bowl, water dish and bed.
practical.safety: Use soft toys only and wash hands after any real animal contact. Never leave children alone with a real pet.

differentiation.support: Feed the toy together and name each need.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what a pet needs every day.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Cares for a toy pet gently
lessons.conclusion: Put the pet to bed and say "Goodnight, Rex."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about how your family cares for a pet or an animal.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say what a pet needs and pretend to care for it" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Kind and gentle
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will show kind and gentle handling of animals.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know that plants and animals are alive and need food, water and care.
resources: Pictures of kind and unkind actions
lessons.starter: Stroke a soft toy slowly and say "Gentle hands. Be kind."
teacherActivities: Show kind actions: stroke, feed, speak softly.
Show pictures and ask "Is it kind?"
Practise holding a toy with two hands.
Say "We are kind to animals" together.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show kind actions: stroke, feed, speak softly. Children: Children copy with a toy.
Step 2. Teacher: Show pictures and ask "Is it kind?" Children: Child says yes or no.
Step 3. Teacher: Practise holding a toy with two hands. Children: Child holds the toy gently.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We are kind to animals" together. Children: Children say the sentence.

practical.title: Gentle hands
steps: Give each child a soft toy.
practical.safety: Use soft toys and remind children never to pull tails or ears. Supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Stroke the toy together with a gentle hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to teach a friend how to be gentle.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is it kind to pull a tail?

lessons.conclusion: Put the toys away and say "We are kind."
lessons.homeConnection: Show gentle hands with pets or toys at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show kind and gentle handling of animals" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Our caring chart
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will use a caring chart for the class plants and toy pet.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know that plants and animals are alive and need food, water and care.
resources: A caring chart with jobs: water, feed, tidy
lessons.starter: Show the chart and say "Every day we care for our plants. Today it is your turn."
teacherActivities: Show the chart and say each job.
Give each child a job for the day.
Put a sticker on the chart.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the jobs.
Child puts a sticker on the chart.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the chart and say each job. Children: Children look and say the jobs.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a job for the day. Children: Child chooses a job.
Step 3. Teacher: Let them do their job. Children: Child waters or tidies.
Step 4. Teacher: Put a sticker on the chart. Children: Child puts a sticker on the chart.

practical.title: Caring jobs
steps: Choose a job on the chart.
Put a sticker on the chart.
practical.safety: Supervise jobs closely and wipe spills. Use child-safe tools only.

differentiation.support: Do the job together and point to the chart.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to remind a friend of their job.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Look at the chart and say "Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Give your child a small caring job at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use a caring chart for the class plants and toy pet" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 caring check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child cares for living things.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know that plants and animals are alive and need food, water and care.
lessons.starter: Sing the caring song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: plants, pets and kind hands.
At each station ask "What does it need?" and watch how the child cares.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: plants, pets and kind hands. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What does it need?" and watch how the child cares. Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy.

practical.title: Caring stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors dry. Use soft toys only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell a friend how to care.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: waters a plant; names what a pet needs; handles toys gently; does a caring job.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
lessons.homeConnection: Keep caring for plants and pets at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child cares for living things" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
